investigation.root_cause: The IUserExits.preConnect() interface signature includes `authHeader?: string` (IUserExits.ts:24). WebLoginComponent.sessionConnect() calls userExitsEventThrower.firePreConnect(createSessionRequest, authHeader) at line 101, where authHeader = 'Basic ' + btoa(username+':'+password) — a base64-encoded credential that is plaintext-equivalent (atob() trivially reverses it). UserExitsEventThrowerService.firePreConnect() (line 40-42) delivers this credential to every registered IUserExits implementation. Any user-exit code (custom integrations, third-party libraries implementing IUserExits) that logs, stores, or transmits the authHeader parameter receives the plaintext-equivalent credential.
investigation.attack_scenario:
Malicious Third-Party User Exit: Developer integrates a third-party analytics or monitoring library that implements IUserExits. Library's preConnect() captures the authHeader parameter: const decoded = atob(authHeader.split(' ')[1]); → 'username:password'. Library exfiltrates credential to vendor server. Every user login is captured.

Accidental Logging: Developer writes a debugging user exit that logs all preConnect parameters including authHeader. The log entry contains 'Basic dXNlcm5hbWU6cGFzc3dvcmQ=' which any log viewer decodes to plaintext credential.

Combined with VULN-004: Malicious generated page displaces existing security hooks (VULN-004), installs credential-capturing user exit, and receives all subsequent login credentials via preConnect.
prerequisites: A user-exit implementation must be registered (any code calling addEventListener(new CustomExit()))
User must attempt to authenticate using ApplinX or LDAP auth method (which generates authHeader)
The user-exit implementer must have code execution capability to exfiltrate data

privilege_boundary.start_privilege: Developer/integrator with ability to register custom IUserExits implementation
privilege_boundary.achieved_privilege: Access to plaintext-equivalent Basic-auth credentials for every ApplinX/LDAP login

impact.description: Plaintext-equivalent credentials (base64 username:password) exposed to all registered user-exit implementations. Any implementation can decode and exfiltrate credentials via atob(authHeader.split(' ')[1]). This enables: password capture for all ApplinX/LDAP authenticated users, credential reuse attacks across systems, account takeover. The OIDC and Natural auth paths do NOT pass authHeader, so the risk is specific to ApplinX/LDAP authentication modes.

sources: WebLoginComponent form fields — username and password entered by user
transformations: forEach(u => u.preConnect(createSessionRequest, authHeader)) — delivered to every listener
sinks: Any IUserExits.preConnect() implementation — can call atob(authHeader.split(' ')[1]) to get 'username:password'
Logging systems if preConnect() logs authHeader parameter
Remote exfiltration via HTTP/WebSocket from malicious user-exit code

direct.impact: API contract exposes credential to all implementers
Distributes credential to all registered implementations without filtering
Source — passes authHeader to event dispatcher

indirect.impact: No credential filtering or masking in default no-op implementation
Malicious generated page can displace security hooks and register credential-capturing exit

remediation_guidance.recommended_fix: Remove the authHeader parameter from the IUserExits.preConnect() interface entirely. User exits do not require raw credentials to function. If connection context is needed by user exits, pass only a sanitized object: { username: string, authMethod: string, timestamp: number } — never the password or auth header. Update all call sites and implementations accordingly.
defense_in_depth: Remove authHeader from preConnect() signature — breaking API change but necessary
If credential context needed, provide: { username, authMethod } — no password
Audit all IUserExits implementations in the codebase for authHeader logging/storage
Add static analysis rule: flag any code accessing authHeader parameter in preConnect()
Document API security contract: preConnect must not log or transmit credential parameters
